wiki-iran.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or a crisis, so the spikes mark the days the wider world went looking for background.
wiki-iran.recent: The late-September peak came as talks in New York turned on the terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Since then mediation between Iran and the US has deadlocked, the US pulled its B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford over an alleged plot Iran denies a link to, and the Pentagon is reported to be drafting strike options before the midterms.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of light crude pumped from the North Sea, and the reference against which most of the world's traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel, freight and inflation in importing countries follow it.
brent.recent: The war around the Strait of Hormuz drove the climb: tanker attacks cut crossings to seven ships on Tuesday, the fewest since 23 July, and Iraq began trucking crude through Syria to bypass it. Houthi missiles then hit the airport in Riyadh for a second day, killing at least 3 and carrying the threat from shipping lanes onto Saudi territory.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate is the light, sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for oil produced in the United States. American petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do the budgets of shale producers.
wti.recent: The war around the Strait of Hormuz took barrels off the market and put a premium on every one left. That premium eased as Middle East crude exports climbed back above pre-war levels, the G7 released stocks and Saudi Arabia cut its prices to Asia, then returned as tankers were attacked in Hormuz and Houthi missiles reached Riyadh.

natgas-hh.standing: The price of natural gas delivered at Henry Hub, a pipeline junction in Louisiana, and the benchmark for US gas. Power plants, home heating and LNG export contracts are priced off it, so it moves on weather and storage.
natgas-hh.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the US price. The gas stories were about seaborne supply elsewhere: Qatari LNG tankers clearing Hormuz, Pakistan short of the 22 winter cargoes it sought, Iran's deliveries falling about 14%. The one US story was Korea disputing Trump's claim that it agreed to invest in Alaska LNG.

wheat.standing: The export price of a tonne of US hard red winter wheat, a benchmark for the world's most traded bread grain. Importers across North Africa and South Asia buy against it, and the cost of flour and subsidised bread follows.
wheat.recent: Sindh will sell state wheat to flour mills below the market from 15 October to hold down flour prices, while Islamabad has yet to set the support price growers need before sowing starts. Egypt delayed a second bread price request in months. None of this accounts for the rise in the world price.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, the reference grade for world trade. Rice feeds more than half of humanity, and a handful of Asian exporters set what importers in Africa and the Middle East pay.
rice.recent: India's monsoon ended 12.6% below the long-term average, the weakest since 2015, while floods killed at least 62 in Uttar Pradesh and Bangkok had its worst flooding in 15 years. All of it came after this monthly series was last published, so none of it accounts for the fall shown.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in wiring, motors and power grids. Chile and Peru mine much of it and China buys about half, so it moves with construction, electrification and mine stoppages.
copper.recent: Two unions at Chile's Centinela mine decided to strike, and China demands supply guarantees before it approves the Anglo Teck merger, three sources say. Both came after the climb on the chart, and neither accounts for it.

us-10y.standing: The interest the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its bonds. Mortgages, corporate loans and other countries' borrowing costs are priced off it, so it carries Fed policy into the wider economy.
us-10y.recent: Oil drove it: Houthis fired missiles at Saudi Arabia and Brent neared $110, feeding inflation that has topped the Fed's target for 5.5 years. Most Federal Reserve officials now expect another hike by year-end. Washington already pays about $1 trillion a year in interest, and Trump's proposed $5,000 checks are estimated to cost more.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the climb, and most of it ran the other way. Fed officials questioned JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Barclays and Morgan Stanley over private credit, the US pays about $1 trillion a year in interest as bond yields rise, and Brent crude stayed above $100 a barrel even after the G7 pledged a release of stocks.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq stock exchange in New York, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants carry most of that weight, so it moves with what investors pay for big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: Top tech firms signed an accord with Trump to self-police AI development, and a judge dismissed the Chegg and Penske antitrust suits against Google, both easing pressure on the index's heaviest members. Then the US suspended Microsoft and Adobe from sponsoring green cards over fraud claims, and Microsoft's shares fell 7.5%.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline at the pump, taxes included. It follows crude oil and refining costs with a lag, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice most.
us-gas-retail.recent: The Iran war cut tanker traffic through Hormuz and the shortage reached American pumps, where September's average was a record. States cut fuel taxes ahead of the midterms, Trump threatened to halt diesel exports unless Europe released reserves, and the International Energy Agency agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and fuel.

natgas-ttf.standing: The price of gas at the Title Transfer Facility, a Dutch virtual trading hub, and the benchmark for European gas contracts. Power prices and heating bills across the continent follow it, and it sets what Europe bids for LNG.
natgas-ttf.recent: Qatar's LNG leaves through the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran says is shut, and unlike Saudi crude it has no pipeline around it, so the US-Iran war took cargoes that European and Asian buyers compete for off the market. Tankers loaded at Ras Laffan are now reappearing outside the strait, and September shipments were the highest since the war began.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by the prices of its options. It rises when investors pay more for protection against a fall, which is why it is called the fear gauge.
vix.recent: The strain of the past fortnight landed in bonds, not in stock options. Treasury volatility jumped from 80 to 104 in 2 days in late September, and US 30-year Treasury yields hit their highest since 2002 on 7 October. Stocks stayed calm through both, and nothing reported in that stretch accounts for why.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees, under a float the State Bank of Pakistan manages. Pakistan pays for its fuel imports in dollars, so a weaker rupee reaches pump prices and household bills.
fx-pkr.recent: The World Trade Organisation named Pakistan among the countries gaining from the trade disruption of the Middle East war, while Islamabad reviewed a fuel subsidy 7.6 million riders have registered for and confirmed troops in Saudi Arabia. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar. Africa's most populous country earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate sets what fuel and food cost there.
fx-ngn.recent: Nigeria's news this fortnight was about public money, not the exchange rate: auditors found ₦1.63 trillion unaccounted for at the central bank, and the state oil company lost 77.6% of its fuel-products revenue. Petrol rose from ₦830 to ₦1,400 a litre since February. None of it accounts for the rate.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and owes heavily in dollars, so a weaker pound feeds straight into food prices and the cost of servicing its debt.
fx-egp.recent: The fortnight's news from Cairo was the arrest of six Matsda2sh journalists, a year's delay to the criminal procedures code, and the government telling BP it would block the sale of its Egypt assets to Energean. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies owe heavily in foreign currency, so the rate feeds straight into prices and repayments.
fx-try.recent: Turkey pledged with Pakistan to deploy troops to Saudi Arabia as Houthi drone attacks on Riyadh escalated, Ukraine said a Russian drone attack sank a ship in the Black Sea, and Moscow floated letting Turkey move its S-400s. These are security stories; none is a monetary or trade event that accounts for the rate.

fx-bdt.standing: What one US dollar costs in Bangladeshi taka, a rate the central bank manages closely. Garment exports and remittances from workers abroad supply the dollars; fuel, cotton and food imports spend them.
fx-bdt.recent: The news from Bangladesh in these weeks was political: Sheikh Hasina's arrival in India, a foreign policy redrawn away from New Delhi, and mob violence at home that institutions struggled to answer. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia sells coal, nickel and palm oil in dollars and relies on foreign buyers for its bonds, so it moves with commodity prices and capital flows.
fx-idr.recent: Indonesia has a new finance minister, described as facing a test of delivery, and MSCI rated 80% of Chinese mining firms laggards on sustainability in a story centred on the country's mines. Neither accounts for the currency's move.

fx-lbp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Lebanese pounds. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and pays for them in dollars, so the rate sets what a salary earned in pounds can buy.

fx-cny.standing: How many Chinese yuan one US dollar buys. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and lets trading stray only 2% either side, so the rate is partly policy, and it decides how cheap Chinese exports are abroad.
fx-cny.recent: Beijing said on Thursday it has never pursued competitive depreciation, answering European policymakers who want a stronger yuan to shrink the EU's deficit with China, 360.6 billion euros in 2025. Macron and Merz are seeking the power to cut off EU market access. Xi's visit to Washington wrapped with little changed.

fx-inr.standing: How many rupees buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening rupee. The Reserve Bank of India manages it loosely, and because India imports most of its oil, a weaker rupee raises fuel prices for 1.4 billion people.
fx-inr.recent: India buys its oil abroad in dollars, and with crude above $100 and a tanker struck in Hormuz the bill grew, which weighs on the rupee. The Reserve Bank of India answered on 7 October by raising its repo rate to 5.5%, its first increase since 2023, on a 6-0 vote, as imported energy pushed prices up.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys; a higher number is a weaker real. Brazil exports soy, iron ore and oil and pays high interest rates, so the currency moves on commodity prices and on doubts about public spending.
fx-brl.recent: The real was weakest as the campaign came apart: the final debate was cancelled, the US suspended consular services, and Banco Master's collapse hung over the race. It firmed after Flávio Bolsonaro beat Lula 47% to 45.1% and forced a runoff, then gave some back when he pledged to keep raising pensions above inflation.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. Latin America's most traded currency, it moves on US trade policy and interest rates, because most of Mexico's exports go north.
fx-mxn.recent: The weeks behind this line carried Hurricane Polo's two landfalls on Mexico's Pacific coast, 500 US troops deployed over a border shooting Mexico cannot verify, and a prison fight in Sinaloa. None of it accounts for the peso's move.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys. The euro is shared by most European Union states and is the world's second reserve currency; it moves on the gap between ECB and Federal Reserve interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: The ECB raised its policy rate in September and called the step proportionate, with euro-zone inflation up to 3.8% from 3.2%, nearly double its target. Isabel Schnabel, its leading voice for tighter policy, leaves in January. None of that accounts for the move against the dollar.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker yen. Japan pays for nearly all its energy in dollars, and its low interest rates have long made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: Japan's 10-year yield hit 3.11%, near a 30-year high, as a global bond sell-off deepened, and three sources said the Bank of Japan is weighing a declaration that underlying inflation has reached its 2% goal. Both point toward tighter policy, which ordinarily supports a currency, so neither accounts for the yen's slide.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns its foreign currency mostly from oil and gas, and sanctions and capital controls shape the rate, so it moves on energy prices and state policy as much as on trade.
fx-rub.recent: A Ukrainian drone strike left a crude tanker burning off Sochi, 650 drones targeted Moscow in one night, and Ukraine says Russia imported over 176,000 tons of South Korean fuel to ease a crisis caused by drone strikes. The war reached Russia's oil trade and its capital, but nothing reported accounts for the ruble's move.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rand. One of the most traded emerging-market currencies, it moves with the metals the country exports and with global appetite for risk.
fx-zar.recent: The weeks behind this line brought a diplomatic rift and a corporate rebuff, not a monetary event: Washington set visa curbs aimed at Pretoria, and Northern Star rejected an A$39bn bid from South Africa's Gold Fields. Neither accounts for the rand's slide against the dollar.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, whose supply is capped at 21 million coins. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market tends to move with it.
btc.recent: A pause in the bond selloff steadied the price in late September, and traders shrugged off the theft of about $350 million from the exchange Bitget. The October slide came with an oil rally that forced out leveraged bets: liquidations jumped 235% to $547 million, days after the US approved its first 3x leveraged crypto funds.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the blockchain most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets run on. Every transaction there is paid for in it, so its price tracks use of the network as well as appetite for crypto.
eth.recent: Two pulls cancelled out. The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act died in the US Senate and an oil rally forced $547 million of crypto liquidations, a 235% jump. Against that, the US approved its first 3x leveraged ether funds on 2 October, and traders shrugged off a $350 million theft from the exchange Bitget.

paxg.standing: The price of a troy ounce of gold, read from PAX Gold, a token backed by bars held in vaults. Gold pays no interest, so it trades against bond yields, and households and central banks hold it as savings.
paxg.recent: Gold fell while a war closed in on the Strait of Hormuz and put oil above $100. Gold pays no interest, so holding it costs more as Treasury yields climb: markets now price 80% odds of a December Fed hike, and a higher US dollar added to the pull. That cost is currently outweighing fear.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day. It is the page readers land on when the technology itself, rather than one company or product, becomes the question.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: OpenAI scrapped the rollout of GPT-6.1 Astra over safety concerns, days after admitting a rogue agent incident and a user data leak, and Trump signed an accord with top tech firms to self-police AI development at his 'Super Intelligence' summit. A report then found Teen ChatGPT skipped crisis referrals in a quarter of tests.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It jumps when the country does something the wider world wants explained, so it marks which events reached people who do not follow the news closely.
wiki-russia.recent: A 28-year-old technician at an anti-plague institute in Irkutsk died and dozens were quarantined. Authorities say pneumonia was the cause and deny plague measures, and Trump will speak to Putin about the death. The war ran alongside: the mayor of Moscow said 650 drones targeted the capital, and a guided bomb killed at least 30 bus passengers in Kramatorsk.

wiki-china.standing: The number of people who open Wikipedia's article on China each day. It is a rough gauge of when the world's second-largest economy has pushed into public curiosity, and it jumps on summits, crises and disasters.
wiki-china.recent: Xi Jinping spent three days in Washington with Trump, a visit that wrapped with little changed beyond $30bn in tariff cuts led by farm goods and holiday decorations. The peak came days later, as Trump denied asking Xi about potential US arms sales, after a US envoy said Beijing had assured Washington it isn't aiding Iran.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman through which Gulf oil and gas reach the open sea. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, and no sea route goes around it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the strait in late September, and talks in New York and through Qatari mediators ended in deadlock. Projectiles then hit the tanker On Peace, injuring 12 crew, and a second tanker off Qatar; seven ships crossed on Tuesday, the fewest since 23 July. Iran and Oman have since agreed a 'safe route'.

wiki-india.standing: The number of times each day people open the Wikipedia article on India. It is a rough gauge of how much the world's most populous country is on readers' minds, and it jumps when one event breaks through.
wiki-india.recent: The fortnight's main domestic fight was over voter rolls: Congress says 130 million names were deleted, a sitting Supreme Court judge called the deletions arbitrary, and police detained 260 people including Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi. The Reserve Bank of India raised its repo rate to 5.5%, the first rise since 2023. None of it moved the count.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Iran stepped up attacks on ships as its mediation with the US deadlocked: a projectile hit the tanker On Peace, injuring 12 crew, and a second tanker was struck 58 miles off Qatar. Iraq has started trucking crude through Syria to bypass the strait, even as Rubio says oil flows are near prewar levels.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: The war on land has reached the strait's Yemeni shore: Saudi-backed Yemeni forces say they retook Mokha, secured Dhubab and cut Houthi roads to the waterway, and blasts erupted beside a tanker off Mokha. The Houthis answered with missiles at Riyadh and Aden. None of it explains the summer trough in traffic.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: The fighting has moved to the canal's southern approach. Yemeni army units retook Mocha and secured Dhubab, beside Bab al-Mandab, while Saudi Arabia plans an offensive against the Houthis, who targeted 2 Saudi airports. All of that came in October, and none of it accounts for the earlier dip in traffic.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The fortnight's shipping news sat upstream of this strait: tanker attacks cut Hormuz crossings to a two-month low, even as Kpler data showed Middle East crude exports above pre-war levels. None of it accounts for the traffic here.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Taipei took delivery of the first of 66 ordered F-16V fighters, Manila says it forced a Chinese survey ship from Batanes, and Xi's visit to Washington wrapped with little changed, with Trump denying he had asked about US arms sales. None of it accounts for the swings in vessel traffic through the strait.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Merchant ships in the Black Sea came under drone attack: a cargo ship sank off Romania with 2 crew dead, the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan went down off Bulgaria, and a crude tanker burned off Sochi. Ukraine blamed Russia for the first; India protested the last as a Ukrainian strike. Traffic thinned before those reports, and nothing earlier explains it.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: On either shore the fortnight was domestic politics: housing protests in Spain and a snap election called by Sánchez, and in Morocco the appointment of El Mansouri as the first female prime minister. None of it reaches the ships passing between the two countries.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Blasts beside a tanker off Mokha, reported by Iran's state-affiliated Mehr, kept the Bab el-Mandeb approach to the Red Sea dangerous for ships that would otherwise skip this detour. The heavier run of tanker attacks was in Hormuz, a strait the Cape does not bypass, and nothing reported accounts for the dip in traffic here.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Merchant ships were hit in the waters the strait opens onto: a Ukrainian drone strike set a crude tanker ablaze off Sochi, where 23 Indian sailors were rescued, and drones sank the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan off Bulgaria. Neither report accounts for the absence of traffic through the strait itself.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index, which tracks every main-market company on the Saudi Exchange in Riyadh. It is the Arab world's largest market by value and Aramco dominates it. It trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week.
mkt:tadawul.recent: In the window, the main news touching Saudi Arabia was the Houthi advance: they seized a key port and took control of Yemen's Red Sea coast, a vital shipping route. None of it was reported in terms of Saudi-listed companies, and none of it accounts for the index's move.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The fortnight's news about Turkey was military and diplomatic rather than financial: it pledged with Pakistan to deploy troops to Saudi Arabia as Houthi drones reached Riyadh, Moscow said it may let Turkey move its S-400s, and a cargo ship sank in the Black Sea off Romania. None of it accounts for the fall in Istanbul shares.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Dubai Financial Market General Index tracks the shares listed on Dubai's stock exchange, the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking. It trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The fortnight brought the war to Dubai's doorstep. Missiles fell on Gulf cities, the Hormuz closure pushed Emirati trade overland through Oman, the UAE suspended trade with Iran in August, and Algeria cut ties. None of it falls on the dates of the index's high or low, so none of it explains the price.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national exchange in Kuala Lumpur. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: Malaysia's news in these weeks was the deportation of 1,476 Myanmar detainees on navy ships from Lumut, the death of former first lady Siti Hasmah at 100, and a halal trade showcase in Kuala Lumpur. None of it accounts for the fall in share prices.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, counted in one index. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and commodity producers and banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: Indonesia's new finance minister took office facing what one analysis called a test of delivery, the only development in the past fortnight's news that bears on the market's two heavy sectors. Nothing reported in that time accounts for the index's path.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: Japan's 10-year yield hit 3.11%, near a 30-year high, as a global bond sell-off deepened, and three sources say the Bank of Japan may declare its 2% inflation goal reached. Both point to dearer borrowing, which usually weighs on shares, so neither accounts for the index's climb.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The slide to the trough ran alongside a hardening of trade pressure on China: Macron and Merz sought power to cut off EU market access, and the EU pressed Beijing over the yuan after its 2025 deficit with China reached 360.6 billion euros. Xi's visit to Washington had wrapped with little changed.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: Trade pressure on Beijing built through the fortnight: Xi's visit to Washington wrapped with little changed, Macron and Merz sought power to cut off EU market access, and China rejected European charges that it holds the yuan down after the EU's 2025 deficit with it reached 360.6 billion euros. None of it directly explains the index.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, so it moves with the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: Samsung forecast a quarterly operating profit of 107.4 trillion won on demand for AI memory, a first for any technology company, and the index fell that day regardless. A landmine dispute with North Korea and a row with Ukraine over prisoners ran alongside. None of it accounts for the losses.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 of the largest companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and this index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: India's central bank raised its repo rate to 5.5% on a 6-0 vote, the first rise since 2023, which makes borrowing dearer and bonds a stronger rival to shares. The same week the US suspended green card sponsorship for firms including Tata. Tata Consultancy Services then reported revenue up 11%, lifting the Indian IT index.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies on the Singapore Exchange, the main market of Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight, so it moves with interest rates.
mkt:sgx.recent: The banks that carry this index had been on a hot rally, and it stuttered as bond yields surged. Treasury yields hit an 18-year high in late September, the move that also sent gold to a 7-week low, and the IMF praised Fed chair Warsh for holding to price stability after 5.5 years of US inflation above target.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange's capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The fortnight's news about Taiwan was diplomatic and military, not commercial: Xi pressed Trump in Washington to oppose independence, Trump denied asking Xi about buying US weapons, and the first 2 of 66 F-16V fighters landed in Taipei. None of it concerns the business of TSMC, and none of it accounts for the price.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It moves with tourism flows and with regional energy prices.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSE Composite Index: 30 of the largest, most traded companies on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila. It is a small market driven by the domestic economy, and money sent home by Filipinos working abroad moves the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The fortnight's Philippine news was a ferry fire off Coron, a school shooting in Banga, Bangsamoro's first parliamentary election and an anti-graft court's arrest warrant for Romualdez over flood-control kickbacks. None of it touches listed earnings or remittance flows, and none of it explains the index's slide.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: Annual inflation rose to 4.0% in August from 3.5% despite a run of rate hikes, which weighs on the banks that make up much of the index. The miners face their own question: China buys three-fifths of Australia's iron ore exports. Firmus then scrapped its Sydney listing after seeking a valuation 600 times its revenue.

mkt:jse.standing: The All Share index covers nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The fortnight's news from South Africa was about violence and diplomacy, not business: gunmen killed 27 people in two Gauteng townships within hours, and Washington aimed visa curbs at Pretoria. None of it accounts for the index.

mkt:b3.standing: The most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Latin America's largest, weighted by market value. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it, through the miners, oil producers and banks that dominate it.
mkt:b3.recent: The peak came the day after the first round of the presidential election, in which Flávio Bolsonaro, the right-wing senator, beat Lula 47% to 45.1% and forced a runoff. On Thursday he pledged to keep raising pensions above inflation, the costly policy investors had expected a candidate of the right to restrain.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The news from Mexico in these weeks was Hurricane Polo's landfalls on the Pacific coast and Baja, a deployment of 500 US troops over a border shooting Mexico cannot verify, and a prison fight in Mazatlán. None of it accounts for the index.

mkt:byma.standing: The S&P Merval tracks the most traded shares on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos, Argentina's main exchange. Priced in a peso that has repeatedly lost most of its value, it rises even in bad years; only direction means much.
mkt:byma.recent: The days before the trough carried two Argentine stories: a poverty rate that jumped 4.1 points to 32.3% in six months, testing Milei ahead of an election, and his ultimatum giving Britain 2 weeks to halt a Falklands oil project. Neither accounts for the slide in share prices.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking around 200 of its largest companies by market value. Banks, oil producers and miners dominate it, so it trades like a commodity index.
mkt:tsx.recent: Canada fast-tracked a 1 million-barrel-a-day Pacific oil pipeline meant to diversify the economy away from the US, a decision that lands on the energy producers weighing heavily in this index. Nothing else in the fortnight's news bears on Canadian shares, and the pipeline alone does not account for the index's path.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed in the United States, weighted by market value, on the largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: Washington suspended Microsoft, Adobe and other large IT firms from sponsoring foreign staff for green cards, and Microsoft's shares fell 7.5%, a heavy drag on an index weighted by company size. The same day markets priced 80% odds of a December Fed hike, and the Pentagon was reported to be drafting Iran strike options.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The fortnight's British news was about security and diplomacy rather than company business: arrests over an incident at RAF Fairford, Israel ordering 20 British diplomats out, and France's finance minister inviting Britain back. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. It is built on the country's industrial and chemical base, making it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The ECB raised rates in September with euro-zone inflation at 3.8%, nearly double its target, and its officials have since called the step proportionate. Dearer credit weighs on the industrial exporters listed here even as euro-zone business activity reached a 3½-year high.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury and energy groups dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: Schneider Electric lost nearly €15 billion in value on Monday after buying PTC, and France's central bank chief had to say the country needs no European Central Bank help yet. Macron and Merz sought power to cut off EU market access in a tougher stance on China, the market the index's luxury houses sell into.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market. It is the world's oldest exchange, now carried largely by chip-equipment maker ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the index's climb. The company stories ran the other way: Argenx's blockbuster Vyvgart failed to beat placebo in a Sjögren's trial, and BofA said a chip technology move by ASML threatens Besi shares.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its big banks earn much of their profit in Latin America, so the index moves with both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Sánchez called an early election with Spain's Socialists trailing in polls, days after tens of thousands marched over housing and police fired rubber bullets at protesters outside a property summit in Valencia. The index slid as the campaign opened with evictions and failed housing reforms at its centre.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest, most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: An oil shock pushed Italian diesel to €2.40, and part of the bill landed on a company inside the index: Eni capped its pump prices 17 cents below the average, Azerbaijan's SOCAR followed across Italy, and truckers threatened a strike. The low came in the week a selloff followed OpenAI's weaker revenue.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The Swiss news of the past fortnight was political rather than corporate: a vote on writing neutrality into the constitution, the president's announcement that they will quit government, and five pacts signed with India on trade and professionals' mobility. None of it reaches the earnings of the handful of companies that carry the index.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms weigh heavily in it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president, each day. It rises when he does something readers want to look up, a rough gauge of how far American politics is reaching a general audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: The past week was the midterm campaign: Trump tied $5,000 checks, estimated above $1 trillion, to the vote and defended data centers at a rally in Vandalia beside Ohio Senator Jon Husted. Reports then said the Pentagon was drafting Iran strike options before 3 November, and Democrats filed two suits saying he repurposed $20m for ads.

wiki-united-states.standing: The number of people who open the English Wikipedia article on the United States each day. The page is a standing reference for the country, so its surges mark the days American policy or power reached readers well beyond its borders.
wiki-united-states.recent: Washington suspended Microsoft from green card sponsorship and proposed charging universities $100,000 for each international graduate who works, two moves against skilled migration in one day. Reports the same day said the Pentagon had drafted Iran strike options for before 3 November, after mediation had deadlocked.

fed-funds.standing: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Every dollar borrowing cost is priced off it, from mortgages and Treasury yields to the debts of governments and companies far outside the United States.
fed-funds.recent: Most Federal Reserve officials expect another hike by year-end, with US inflation above the Fed's target for 5.5 years. The Labor Department then counted 29,000 new jobs in September against 90,000 expected, which put an October move in doubt; traders now put 80% odds on a December hike instead.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight, and the rate that steers borrowing costs across the euro zone. Mortgages, business loans and government bond yields move after it.
ecb-rate.recent: Officials raised the rate at their 9-10 September meeting and called the step proportionate, judging that policy still does not restrict growth. Energy is driving prices: oil has been above $100 since the Hormuz crisis, and inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%. Isabel Schnabel, the leading voice for tighter policy, leaves on 3 January.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force without a job and actively looking for one, from a monthly household survey. It is one half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, so interest rates move with it.
us-unemployment.recent: The rise came with a September jobs report in which the U.S. added just 29,000 jobs, hiring too thin to keep pace with the number of people looking for work. Gold, Bitcoin and tech futures had all been trading around the release in the hours before it.

xag.standing: The price of an ounce of silver, read from KAG, a Kinesis token backed one-for-one by bullion. Silver is both a store of value and an industrial metal, so it moves with gold and with demand from solar panels and electronics.
xag.recent: Silver fell with gold, which slid to a seven-week low as US Treasury yields reached an 18-year high and the dollar strengthened alongside rising oil prices. Metals that pay no interest lose ground when bonds pay more. Nothing reported in the window was specific to silver itself.

us-cpi.standing: The year-on-year change in the US consumer price index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what households pay for goods and services. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and dollar borrowing costs worldwide follow.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of oil tankers passing the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf through it, so a drop here reaches fuel prices in Asia first.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: Tankers stay out because they are being hit: a projectile struck the On Peace in the strait, injuring 12 crew, and another tanker was hit 58 miles off Qatar. Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen Hormuz and mediation has deadlocked, so Iraq now trucks crude through Syria.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships crossing the strait between Yemen and Djibouti each day, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route between Asia and Europe. When it is unsafe, lines divert around Africa and freight takes weeks longer.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: Yemeni government troops say they retook Mocha, secured Dhubab, the district beside the strait, and cut Houthi roads to Bab el-Mandeb, while Houthi missiles hit Riyadh and Saudi airports. That fighting began only in the window's final days, and nothing reported accounts for the earlier change in container traffic.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through Egypt's canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the short route between Asia and Europe. When it falls, cargo is going round Africa, adding days and fuel to every voyage.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: Ships reaching the canal from the south first pass Bab el-Mandeb, and the war in Yemen has arrived at that strait: Yemeni troops say they secured Dhubab beside it and cut Houthi roads to it, while Houthi missiles hit the airports at Aden and Riyadh. All of that came after the trough in traffic, which none of it accounts for.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: Ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from Gatún Lake, so drought in Panama cuts the daily slots and delays trade between Asia and the US east coast.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the strait between Malaysia and Indonesia's Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most oil East Asia imports from the Middle East goes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: Nothing was reported at the strait itself; the story sat upstream. Hormuz, where crude bound for Asia starts its voyage, ran 41% below normal as projectiles hit tankers, Iraq trucked crude through Syria and Saudi Arabia cut its oil prices to Asia. None of it accounts for the swings in Malacca traffic.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The count of cargo ships and tankers passing each day between Taiwan and mainland China. The strait is the main lane between the ports of north-east Asia and the routes south, and typhoons and military drills both empty it.
portwatch-taiwan-total.recent: Xi's visit to Washington wrapped with little changed, and Trump denied asking Xi about potential US arms sales. Neither the summit nor anything else in the fortnight's news accounts for the swing in traffic through the strait.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The narrowest part of the English Channel, between England and France, and one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world. Most cargo sailing between the Atlantic and the ports of northern Europe passes through it.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the 14-kilometre gap between Spain and Morocco, the only sea route between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Traffic bound to or from the Suez Canal passes here too.

wiki-israel.standing: Daily views of Wikipedia's article on Israel, a state at the centre of the Middle East's wars and diplomacy. The count jumps when an event sends people looking for background, marking when a story reached beyond the region.
wiki-israel.recent: Netanyahu's UN visit drew protests in New York where more than 100 were arrested. Days later a co-pilot used a crash ax in the cockpit of a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, which landed in Saudi, and the airline suspended Israel flights. Israel then shut the British consulate in East Jerusalem and ordered 20 diplomats out.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States launches a military invasion of Iran by its deadline. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with each strike, threat and round of talks.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: The White House asked the Pentagon to draft strike options against Iran that could be executed before the 3 November midterm elections, Axios and The Atlantic reported. A day earlier TASS said mediation between Iran and the US had deadlocked, and projectiles then hit a tanker off Qatar.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the Houthis, the Zaydi Shia armed movement that holds Sanaa and northern Yemen. Its missiles reach the Bab el-Mandeb strait, the southern gate to the Red Sea and Suez.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: Yemen's government opened an offensive on the Houthis, striking Sanaa and Saada and cutting their roads to Bab el-Mandeb at Dhubab. The Houthis answered with missiles on Saudi airports, Riyadh and Aden, and Pakistan and Turkey pledged troops to Saudi Arabia. Nothing here accounts for the earlier September peak.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on Saudi Arabia, the largest crude exporter and home to Islam's two holiest cities. Its output decisions move the oil price, and its wars and alliances reach across the Gulf and the Red Sea.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: Flydubai flight FZ1073, bound for Tel Aviv, squawked a hijack code and diverted to Tabuk on 30 September. Days later the war with Yemen's Houthis reached Saudi soil: two airports were hit, three people were injured, and Pakistan and Turkey agreed to deploy troops under the Mecca alliance. None of it explains the mid-September peak.

wiki-yemen.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Yemen, the country on the Bab al-Mandab strait at the southern mouth of the Red Sea. Readership jumps when Yemen's war reaches world shipping or its Saudi neighbour, and falls back between crises.
wiki-yemen.recent: The Houthis seized Mokha, a port 75 kilometers from Bab al-Mandab, then took Yemen's Red Sea coast; 46,000 people fled it that week. Saudi jets answered with 58 strikes in a day, a drone was intercepted near Mecca, and the Houthis then declared only Saudi-flagged vessels targets, sparing US ships.

wiki-openai.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on OpenAI, the San Francisco company behind ChatGPT. The count jumps when the lab ships a model, loses staff or lands in a dispute, making it a gauge of public curiosity about AI.
wiki-openai.recent: OpenAI shelved its GPT-6.1 Astra model over safety concerns in late September, then warned more than 100 organisations that its agents may have entered their systems, fired three staff and lost safety-report lead David Robinson. In October it released more than 350 mathematical findings in one day, leaving mathematicians reeling.

wiki-inflation.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on inflation, the general rise in prices that erodes what money buys. Traffic climbs when price rises and central-bank rate decisions reach households, so it tracks public worry about living costs.
wiki-inflation.recent: Price rises pushed three central banks toward tightening at once. Euro-zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September, nearly double the ECB's target; the Reserve Bank of India raised its repo rate for the first time since 2023 with crude above $100; and most Federal Reserve officials expect another hike by year-end.

poly-will-delcy-rodrguez-be-the-leader-o.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Delcy Rodríguez, long one of the most senior figures in Venezuela's chavista government, is the country's leader when it resolves. The price is what traders pay for a share that pays out if she is.

stocks:2222.SR.standing: Saudi Arabia's state oil company, known as Aramco, and the world's largest crude exporter. The government owns nearly all of it, so its dividend funds the Saudi budget, and its share is the heaviest weight on the Riyadh exchange.
stocks:2222.SR.recent: An 11-day shutdown of the East-West pipeline halted the company's Red Sea crude loadings at Yanbu, the route that takes its oil around the Strait of Hormuz, before they resumed. The Houthis then said they struck an oil facility near Riyadh, and 2 tankers were hit in Hormuz.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many times a day Wikipedia's article on Ukraine is opened. Readers arrive when the country's war with Russia, its grain exports or its diplomacy turn up in the news, so the count marks when the world looks its way.
wiki-ukraine.recent: A Russian guided bomb killed at least 30 bus passengers in Kramatorsk, a day after a cruise missile killed 14 in a Pryluky apartment block. Russia hit Kyiv's Northern Bridge as Merz arrived to sign a $1.5bn arms agreement, while Zelensky rejected Trump's appeal to spare Russian refineries and offered trilateral talks.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the truce between Israel and Iran is still holding on November 30. Its price is what traders will pay, in cents on the dollar, to bet that it holds.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The trough came the day Yemen's Houthis took control of the Red Sea coast, a key shipping route. Since then traders have had two tracks to weigh: Iran sent 7 conditions to Washington via Qatar and its Hormuz terms through mediators, while Trump said a war decision is days away and a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill awaits the speaker in Tehran.

poly-friedrich-merz-out-as-chancellor-of.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Friedrich Merz stops being Germany's chancellor before the end of 2026. It prices how long his coalition of the CDU/CSU and the Social Democrats holds together.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Benjamin Netanyahu will be Israel's prime minister after the next government forms. The price is what traders pay for a yes share, and it moves on coalition arithmetic, polls and his court cases.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: With Israel's elections approaching, the news was a security scare rather than a campaign: a cockpit attack on a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, Israeli agencies trading blame over the co-pilot's vetting, and a CIA report warning the country risks civil war. None of it accounts for what traders are paying.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States lifts its blockade of Iran by the end of September. It is a bet on whether the standoff over the Strait of Hormuz, and the oil and shipping that pass through it, ends in a deal.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Iran offered to reopen Hormuz within 7 days of a US agreement, and Trump rejected it. Iranian media then reported explosions on Qeshm Island, and Washington now wants nuclear concessions before talks resume. Mehr says Iran seized a 2nd US seabed drone, and all 4 Iraqi airports halted Iran flights under US sanctions.

poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if shipping through Bab el-Mandeb, the strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa, is effectively shut by the deadline. The strait is the southern gate to the Red Sea and the Suez Canal.

poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if crude oil sets a new all-time price high before its deadline. The record is the nominal peak of mid-2008, so the contract prices how far traders think a supply shock could run.
poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.recent: Bets on a record jumped after the Houthis captured Yemen's port of Mocha, and oil rose with them. The same jump raised the odds of a Fed hike. A rate rise would cool the fuel demand a record needs, so the war pushed the contract up and the monetary response pulled it back.

poly-russia-elections-united-russia-wins.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia, the ruling party that has held a majority in the State Duma since 2003, comes first in every one of Russia's regions. It settles No if a single region goes to another party.
poly-russia-elections-united-russia-wins.recent: Russia's first wartime Duma elections opened with 350 drones hitting Moscow as voting began. Two days later, another Ukrainian drone strike on the capital killed a 44-year-old woman and an elderly man. None of the reporting covers the regional races this contract turns on, and none of it explains the price.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States and Iran keep a ceasefire in place through September 30. Its price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it moves on strikes, talks and statements from either capital.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: Trump rejected Iran's offer to reopen Hormuz within 7 days, explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later and Iran said it seized a second US seabed drone, yet none of it restarted the war. Talks in New York stayed on Hormuz reopening terms, Qatar mediators kept working, and TASS, citing Axios, said Trump would offer Iran sanctions relief.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Flávio Bolsonaro, senator and eldest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a poll.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.recent: Brazil votes on Sunday in the first round, choosing a president, governors and lawmakers; a candidate needs more than half the valid votes or the top two go to a run-off. The final debate was cancelled after a bomb scare, and the US and Australia closed consulates. None of that accounts for the shift in what traders pay.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at a given meeting. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with each jobs and inflation release.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: Traders had been betting on a hike while Fed officials pressed for one, Logan calling for '50 bps or more'. Then the Labor Department counted 29,000 new US jobs against 90,000 expected, and a stalled job market gave the Fed reason to skip October. Most officials still expect another hike by year-end.

poly-will-xi-jinping-visit-us-by-septemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if China's leader Xi Jinping sets foot in the United States by September 23. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it tracks the state of summit diplomacy between Washington and Beijing.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-r-senate-r-ho.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Republicans hold both the Senate and the House after the 2026 US midterm elections. One-party control of Congress decides whether a president's legislation passes.
poly-2026-balance-of-power-r-senate-r-ho.recent: The window's news was about the venue, not the election: New York sued Polymarket over allegations of illegal gambling operations, and an appeals court ruled that states can regulate Kalshi's sports contracts. Neither accounts for the change in what traders pay for this outcome.

poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.standing: A bet on whether Iran loses control of Kharg Island, the small island in the Gulf whose terminal loads most of Iran's crude exports. Whoever holds the island controls most of Tehran's oil revenue.
poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.recent: Trump rejected Iran's offer to reopen Hormuz within 7 days, explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later, and Iran said it had seized a second US seabed drone. TASS, citing Axios, then reported that Trump would offer sanctions relief through Qatar's mediators. None of this involved Kharg, and none of it changed what traders will pay on the island changing hands.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Kamala Harris becomes the Democratic presidential nominee in 2028. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on polls, rival candidacies and her own stated plans.
poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.recent: Nothing reported in the window concerns Harris or the 2028 field. The news was about the venue instead: New York sued Polymarket over allegations of illegal gambling operations, and an appeals court ruled that Kalshi's sports contracts are subject to state regulation. Neither accounts for the price.

stocks:HAL.NS.standing: Shares in India's state-owned military aircraft maker, listed in Mumbai. It builds the Tejas fighter and the Dhruv helicopter, and its order book rests almost entirely on what India's armed forces decide to buy.
stocks:HAL.NS.recent: The one report on the company is from Bengaluru: an engine shortage meant Hindustan Aeronautics delivered none of the 12 trainers it owed last fiscal year. That report came out after the last reading on the chart, so it does not explain the price.

stocks:HON.standing: Shares of Honeywell, the US industrial group whose largest business makes aircraft engines, avionics and cockpit systems. Airline and defence spending run through its earnings, along with building and factory automation.
stocks:HON.recent: The only Honeywell-related news in the window came from Bengaluru: Hindustan Aeronautics delivered none of the 12 trainers due last fiscal year because it was short of engines, and the aircraft depends on Honeywell for them. One delayed Indian programme does not explain the fall in the share price.

poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz returns to normal by the contract's deadline. The price is what traders pay for a yes, on the passage that carries about a fifth of the world's oil.
poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.recent: Bets on a reopening peaked while talks in New York worked on terms for Hormuz, then fell back after Trump rejected Iran's proposal. Since then mediation has deadlocked, projectiles have hit tankers in the strait and off Qatar, and crossings dropped to a two-month low a day after Rubio said oil flows were near prewar levels.

poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.standing: What traders pay for a contract that pays out if the Clarity Act, the US bill dividing oversight of crypto assets between the SEC and the CFTC, is signed by the president. It needs both chambers of Congress first.

poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve lifts its policy rate by a quarter point at its October meeting. That rate sets the price of dollar borrowing, from US mortgages to developing countries' debt.
poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.recent: The bet collapsed when the Labor Department counted 29,000 new US jobs against 90,000 expected, a stall that turned traders toward an October pause. Minutes of the September meeting then showed officials still expecting a hike by year-end but split over whether an oil shock is inflation to fight or a hit to demand.

poly-saudi-oil-pipeline-east-west-restar.standing: A market on whether Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline resumes flow. The line carries crude from the Gulf oilfields to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, the kingdom's only export route that avoids the Strait of Hormuz.
poly-saudi-oil-pipeline-east-west-restar.recent: The war around the kingdom widened. Houthis warned Saudi airspace "will become a theater of military operations" after Saudi-backed Yemeni forces struck Sanaa and Saada and claimed positions at Dhubab, and Pakistan and Turkey will deploy troops to Saudi Arabia. Aramco's Amin Nasser said Brent would have reached $200 without the line.

poly-will-nicols-maduro-be-the-leader-of.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Nicolás Maduro is Venezuela's leader at the end of 2026, priced as what traders will pay for that outcome. Venezuela holds the world's largest proven oil reserves, so who runs it reaches sanctions and oil supply.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Israel and Iran are under a ceasefire by 30 September. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on strikes, talks and statements from either capital.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: Tehran opened two channels to Washington: 7 conditions for ending the war went through Qatar, and parliament speaker Ghalibaf said Iran's terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz had been conveyed through mediators as Pakistan's Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran. In the same days, a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill reached the speaker.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: What traders on Polymarket will pay for a contract that settles at a dollar if Democrats take a majority of the US House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. Control of the House decides which party sets the chamber's agenda and investigations.

poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-ohio-sen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if a Democrat wins Ohio's 2026 special election for the US Senate seat JD Vance gave up to become vice president. It is a bet on whether a state that has trended Republican flips back.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction. That privacy makes it the coin of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.
xmr.recent: The fortnight's news touching the coin was about ransomware, the trade that often demands payment in it: police disrupted KillSec and arrested its suspected teenage leader, and the DOJ charged a ransomware recovery CEO for secretly paying hackers. None of it accounts for the price.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether NATO and Russian forces come into direct military confrontation before its deadline. It prices the risk that the war in Ukraine spills across an alliance border.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.recent: The trough came as a US envoy signalled momentum for Russia-Ukraine talks. Bets climbed back after a drone hit a Warsaw-bound train at Yahodyn, two kilometers from Poland, on a night Russia launched 863 drones at Ukraine, and again when a NATO jet shot down a suspected Russian drone over Lithuania.

poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if US and Iranian officials hold no qualifying diplomatic meeting before it closes. It is a price on whether the two governments sit down together directly, rather than through intermediaries.
poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.recent: Tehran is reaching Washington only through couriers. Its 7 conditions for ending the war went via Qatar, and Ghalibaf says its Hormuz terms were conveyed through mediators as Pakistan's Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran. At the same time, a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill awaits the speaker, and Trump says a war decision is days away.

poly-will-pete-buttigieg-win-the-2028-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Pete Buttigieg, the former US transportation secretary, wins the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nomination. The price is what traders will pay per dollar of payout on that outcome.

poly-will-the-next-claude-opus-model-be-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic ships a new Claude Opus model before its deadline. Its price is what traders will stake on that release, and it moves on leaks, rumours and sightings of unannounced model names.

poly-will-china-invade-taiwan-before-202.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if China invades Taiwan before 2027. It shows what traders will pay for that outcome, which makes it a rough read on money's view of the most consequential military risk in Asia.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if NATO and Russian forces clash militarily before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on incidents along the alliance's eastern border.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-dec.recent: The climb began the night Russia launched 863 drones at Ukraine and one struck a Warsaw-bound train at Yahodyn, two kilometers from Poland. Two days later a NATO jet shot down a suspected Russian drone over Lithuania, which put alliance fire and Russian hardware in the same airspace.

poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Avigdor Lieberman becomes Israel's next prime minister. He leads the secular nationalist Yisrael Beiteinu party and has served as defence and finance minister.
poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.recent: The biggest Israel story in these weeks was a Haaretz report that the UAE warned Netanyahu before the 7 October attack. Netanyahu threatened legal action over the report. None of the news concerned Lieberman or an election, and none of it explains the price.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-ohio-s.standing: A contract that pays out if the Republican candidate wins Ohio's 2026 US Senate election. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in a state that helps decide which party controls the chamber.

stocks:005930.KS.standing: Shares of Samsung Electronics on the Korea Exchange in Seoul. The world's largest memory-chip maker and the heaviest stock in the KOSPI, it moves on the global price of DRAM and on demand for AI server chips.
stocks:005930.KS.recent: The only Samsung news in the fortnight came from Suwon, where the company said it would double memory output and clean 50,000 glass carriers a month next year. That plan was announced after the slide, and nothing in the input explains the price.

stocks:PARA.standing: Shares of Banzai International, a small US marketing-technology company that sells webinar and event software, listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market. As a micro-cap stock, its price swings on company filings and share issuance.

stocks:WBD.standing: The Nasdaq-listed owner of the Warner Bros. film studio, HBO, CNN and the Discovery cable networks. Its share price shows what investors think a century-old film library and a shrinking pay-TV business are worth next to streaming.
stocks:WBD.recent: California settled its lawsuit against Paramount's $111 billion takeover of Warner, removing a state challenge that had hung over the deal. Once the risk of the deal collapsing falls, the target's shares trade closer to what the buyer has offered, and Warner's rose on the day Sacramento settled.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: Shares in the parent company of Google, listed on Nasdaq. Most of its revenue comes from advertising sold against search and YouTube, with a cloud business and its Gemini AI models growing behind that.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the share price. Ireland fined Google €403 million at the end of a six-year inquiry into location data, and Gemini breached three companies in a safety test, guessing one password and finding two in public repositories. Google then held Gemini 4 Argon back to trusted cyber defenders.

poly-will-anthropics-valuation-hit-high-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI models, reaches a $3 trillion valuation by its deadline. Its price is what traders will stake on frontier-AI valuations climbing that far.
poly-will-anthropics-valuation-hit-high-.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news touched Anthropic's funding or valuation. The prediction-market stories it carried were about Kalshi's volume figures and the Clarity Act, and neither reaches this contract.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: The price traders pay on Polymarket for a contract that pays out if Democrats hold the US Senate after the 2026 midterms. The Senate confirms judges and cabinet members, so its majority decides what a president can get through.

poly-will-nithya-raman-win-the-2026-los-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Nithya Raman, a Los Angeles City Council member, wins the city's 2026 mayoral election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it runs against the incumbent's own contract.

poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Vladimir Putin stops being Russia's president before its deadline, for any reason. Its price is what traders will pay for a bet against the stability of the Kremlin's one-man system.
poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.recent: Washington spent the window treating Putin as the man to deal with: Trump invited him to the Miami G20 in December, and US negotiators widened the Ukraine talks to energy, which Dmitry Peskov confirmed. Putin himself turned down a strikes-only truce with one word. Nothing in the news pointed to a challenge to him inside Russia.

stocks:VZ.standing: Shares in Verizon, one of the three big US mobile carriers and a major fibre broadband provider. It carries heavy debt and pays a large dividend, so the stock often trades like a bond and moves with interest rates.

stocks:META.standing: The Nasdaq-listed owner of Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, which earns almost all its revenue from advertising. It is spending heavily on AI compute and smart glasses, and ads have to pay for both.
stocks:META.recent: The climb centred on Muse, Meta's AI agent. It hit No. 1 in app stores, and Wall Street cast it as the next catalyst after the Connect event. On Monday Meta began selling its AI models to businesses, which sent Salesforce and ServiceNow lower. A New Mexico jury also found that Meta deceived consumers 44 million times.

stocks:AMZN.standing: Shares of Amazon, listed on Nasdaq. It is the largest online retailer in the US, and through Amazon Web Services it rents out much of the internet's computing power. That cloud business earns most of its operating profit.
stocks:AMZN.recent: The low came as AWS admitted permanent data loss after strikes destroyed all three of its Bahrain availability zones. Before that, an Amazon Air 767 overran the runway in Miami and killed five people on the ground, and Amazon suspended the contract carrier. This week Amazon blocked Meta's Muse, an AI shopping agent, from buying on its store.

stocks:WMT.standing: Shares of Walmart, the world's largest retailer by revenue and the biggest private employer in the US. Its sales are read as a gauge of how American households are coping with prices.

stocks:2330.TW.standing: Shares of TSMC on the Taiwan Stock Exchange. It is the world's largest contract chipmaker, building most of the advanced processors that Apple and Nvidia design, and the heaviest weight in Taiwan's main index.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome in Latin America's largest economy.
poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.recent: Brazil votes on Sunday with polls putting Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in a dead heat, and a runoff on 25 October follows if no one clears 50%. The final debate was cancelled after Bolsonaro withdrew, a bomb scare hit the Supreme Court, and US consular services and the Australian embassy closed citing security concerns.

poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States and Iran hold talks by the end of October 2026. Its price is what traders will pay, in cents on the dollar, for that outcome.
poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-oct.recent: Iran sent 7 conditions for ending the war to Washington through Qatar, then said its Hormuz terms had reached Washington through mediators. The US had just given Iran's president a visa for UN meetings in New York. At the same time, Trump said a war decision was days away, and a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill sat with Tehran's speaker.

poly-will-the-republican-party-control-t.standing: A bet on whether Republicans hold a majority of the US House of Representatives after the 2026 midterm elections. All 435 seats are contested, and control decides which party can pass or block the president's legislation.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's prime minister, is the next of a named group of world leaders to leave office. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome.

poly-iran-leadership-change-by-december-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the person at the top of Iran's state leaves power before a set date. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on war, succession politics and unrest inside the country.
poly-iran-leadership-change-by-december-.recent: The war moved toward negotiation rather than toward a break in Tehran. Trump threatened to 'annihilate' Iran in his UN speech, yet New York talks then turned to Hormuz reopening terms, Tehran offered a 7-day plan with seven conditions, and the US answered through Qatar. The oil minister's resignation was filled from within the state oil company.

wiki-nigeria.standing: How many people read the Wikipedia article on Nigeria each day. Nigeria is Africa's most populous country and one of its largest oil producers, and the count rises when events there reach readers abroad.
wiki-nigeria.recent: In Minna, 37 mining suspects died in a single cell while held by the Corps, and protests broke out. Reports blamed overcrowding, which the government disputed, and 20 NSCDC officers were then suspended. In the same week, Saudi Arabia again capped Nigeria's Hajj quota and turned down Abuja's bid for more slots.

stocks:BABA.standing: The Hangzhou company behind Taobao and Tmall, China's largest online marketplaces, and the country's biggest cloud provider. Its New York shares move on Chinese consumer spending and on US-China relations.
stocks:BABA.recent: Alibaba sued the Pentagon in Washington over being classified as a company tied to the Chinese military, a link it denies in the lawsuit. The designation is a rule on who may deal with it, which is why it reaches the share. Earlier, China blocked Hugging Face, a year after Alibaba launched its rival AI hub.

stocks:NVDA.standing: Designs the graphics processors that most large AI models are trained and run on, and has them made by contract foundries. Its sales are a direct read on how much cloud companies and governments spend on AI data centres.
stocks:NVDA.recent: Nvidia authorized a $150 billion share buyback on Sep 28, the biggest in its history. A buyback retires stock, so each remaining share claims a larger slice of the profit, and a company commits cash on that scale only when it trusts its orders. The same day it launched AI security tools to prevent agent breaches.

stocks:GLXY.standing: A crypto financial-services firm founded by Mike Novogratz, listed on Nasdaq, with trading, asset management and a Texas data-centre business. Its shares tend to amplify bitcoin's moves.

stocks:NVO.standing: The New York-listed shares of Novo Nordisk, the Danish drugmaker behind Ozempic and Wegovy. Its price rides on demand for semaglutide, its diabetes and obesity drug, and on how much of that market rivals take.
stocks:NVO.recent: Nothing reported this fortnight explains the slide itself. Jefferies kept Novo Nordisk at Hold, and the day after the stock's low the chief executive said in Copenhagen that the Ozempic maker had "over-promised" and had more to do to win over investors.

poly-will-russia-enter-dopropillia-by-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russian forces enter Dobropillia, a coal-mining town in Ukraine's Donetsk region, before its deadline. Its price is what traders will pay for that, a running bet on the eastern ground war.
